substantiveDifference: Addresses effective flood map versus actual observed house history even without current damage, with Harris County mapping limitations, dated map capture and evidence reconciliation. Existing flood-damage guide concerns pricing/remediation; insurance guide concerns claim proceeds, not map/history interpretation.

faq.q: Does being outside the mapped floodplain prove a house never flooded?
faq.a: No. Harris County Flood Control District explains that local ponding and overland flow can occur beyond mapped bayou or creek floodplains. A mapped designation and a property history answer different questions.

faq.q: Is the Harris County Flood Education Mapping Tool the effective FIRM?
faq.a: No. HCFCD says its educational tool displays mapped information but is not the effective Flood Insurance Rate Map. Its guidance directs users to FEMA Map Service Center for the effective map.

faq.q: Can a neighborhood flood map establish what happened inside my house?
faq.a: The map alone does not document that. Separate your known observations, property-specific reports, photographs and repair records from the map information, and identify what remains unknown.

faq.q: Can Cash As-Is evaluate a property with unresolved flood questions?
faq.a: You can explain what is known and what records remain under review when asking for an offer evaluation. Any proposal depends on the property and agreement; neither a cash offer nor a map substitutes for accurate information and applicable disclosures.
